claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are governed jointly by composition-dependent transition temperature and processing-induced microstructure.
Melt spinning will refine the alloy grain size.
Melt spinning will produce a higher defect density.
Grain size influences the magnetostructural transition and magnetocaloric response.
Defect density influences the magnetostructural transition and magnetocaloric response.
Changes in alloy composition alter the transition temperature.
Processing-induced microstructure modifies the first-order magnetostructural transition.
The modified transition produces a more gradual entropy change.
The modified transition produces a more reversible entropy change.
Controlled processing will reduce hysteretic losses by 20% relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Controlled processing will increase the magnetocaloric response, measured through entropy change, by 15% relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The predicted effects hold for Fe contents of 20–40 at.%, Mn contents of 20–40 at.%, Ni contents of 10–30 at.%, and grain sizes below 1 μm.
The test is to be performed at applied fields no greater than 1 T and temperatures of 250–350 K.
The exact relationship between microstructure and magnetocaloric response is not well understood.
Optimal processing conditions for producing the desired microstructure have not been established.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a 15% increase in magnetocaloric entropy change, whereas the falsification rule is framed around failure to obtain at least a 10% reduction in entropy change. The direction of the required ΔS change is therefore inconsistent.
